citation.title: Roentgenographic cephalometric study of 128 children with normal occlusion in Shanghai (author's translation)
citation.journal: Chung-Hua Kou Chiang Ko Tsa Chih (Chinese Journal of Stomatology)

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08: norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 17 differences (logs/task9a2-compare-<id>.log). Every mean and SD of both extractors re-read from the page images (PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24), and the settled file checked by script against a third, independent reading of the pages (the table in sets.test.ts). Decisions: (0) Source text normalised to one pattern giving table, page, row and column with sex and age (a and b worded it differently; prose only). b's UFH:LFH% rows (#29) not entered: the merge notes rule the printed UFH:LFH ratio is not a catalogue measurement (do not compute ratios). (1) a's Y axis males 13 y 66 ± 3 rejected: on Table III p. 22 the Y axis (66 ± 3) and facial axis (84 ± 3) values sit in the Fu columns, right-aligned at the right edge of the males and females groups, not in Lou's (b did not enter it). (2) Selection a unknown / b class-I-balanced -> class-I-balanced: chosen by occlusion and profile (text p. 21). Page images: PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24 (Tables I-VI), rendered at 2000 px.

caveats: Quoted second-hand from Moate & Darendeliler 2002 (Aust Orthod J 18:19-26, a compilation of published Chinese cephalometric norms), Table III; the original paper was not read. The compilation rounds every mean and SD to whole numbers (Lew's soft tissue to 0.5) and gives no landmark, plane or method definitions.
The compilation states no film scale or magnification for any study; assumed true size (owner ruling M-2).

128 Chinese students in Shanghai selected on occlusion and profile (the title says normal occlusion), aged 10 and 13 years (text p. 21). Only 13-year values are tabled (Table III); group sizes are not given.
Not entered (not catalogue measurements; no ratio computed): N-ANS and UFH:LFH%.
Table V (p. 24) averages several studies; it is not entered for this study (merge notes).
